an9.47:0.3: Extinguishment Is Apparent in the Present Life
an9.47:1.1: “Reverend, they say that ‘extinguishment is apparent in the present life’.
an9.47:1.2: In what way did the Buddha say extinguishment is apparent in the present life?”
an9.47:2.1: “First, take a bhikkhu who, fully withdrawn from sensual pleasures … enters and dwells in the first stage of meditation.
an9.47:2.2: To this extent the Buddha said that extinguishment is apparent in the present life in a qualified sense. …
an9.47:3.1: Furthermore, take a bhikkhu who, going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, enters and dwells in the cessation of perception and feeling. And, having seen with wisdom, their defilements come to an end.
an9.47:3.2: To this extent the Buddha said that extinguishment is apparent in the present life in a definitive sense.”
